details:
I feel like we need more prioritisation on animator performance for avatars. Not everyone has a Ryzen x3D chip and I'm inclined to say that animator performance is the biggest reason low FPS is still an issue in VRChat.

These new recent updates have been a great step in the right direction such as the new VRC constraints, but now I'd love to see more focus on ways creators can optimize their animators. I would love to make my animator more optimized without having to sacrifice certain features on my personal avatar but I have hit a limit of what I can do.

One of the main offenders for this is definitely face tracking because of the local smoothing systems they rely on. On my system that runs an AMD Ryzen 5950X there is a difference of around 7 FPS between an avatar that doesn't have face tracking installed on it, and an avatar that does using OSCsmooth. This seems to affect both local and remote players, though it's worse for the local player. Not a scientific test obviously but it's very measurable in my case.

If animator performance could somehow be improved it would give users some serious performance gains. I'm personally in a situation where I am pretty much always CPU bottlenecked. My GPU is never the issue, and I know the same can be said for many other users. And the saddest thing is in instances where I may be getting 20-30fps with everyone shown, I can just disable all animations for every trust rank which disables the animators and be at almost 90FPS despite shaders etc. still showing.

I think there are a few things that could be looked into to help creators improve their animator performance. Here are some ideas:

- Smoothing parameters + Lower resolution floats: We could have some additional settings in the SDK that let us mark a parameter as a smoothed parameter. If marked as smoothed it should linearly smoothly interpolate between values. Having the ability to change the smoothing value for the local player and remote player is an absolute must too. This being part of the SDK/Game engine instead of on avatar animators would hugely improve performance for face tracked avatars. We would also need some kind of replacement for binary parameters as all face tracking users rely on them for saving parameters, but this inadvertently adds animator complexity too. Being able to change the amount of bits a float value uses at the cost of it's accuracy would be a good solution to this.

- Layer skipping: Right now we have the ability to set layer weights via a state component, but setting a layer to 0 doesn't actually skip it from updating on the CPU. If it did this could allow for some major animator optimisations for creators.

- Multithreading: The most obvious one, but I know its a lot easier said than done because of thread synchronisation issues. But having some kind of multithreading support would probably just fix most, if not all FPS issues that are associated with avatar animators. I am under the assumption that all loaded avatars in a scene all run their animators on the same CPU thread. I've always wondered if each loaded avatars animator could run on a different thread instead? At least for their FX layers or something. So the entire processor is doing something instead of just one thread getting absolutely hammered by a few avatar animators running.

- In game profiling: Having some sort of in game performance profiling would be great. The unity profiler does not seem to replicate VRChat performance behaviour. I've had animators that within unity seem performant, but for some reason in game they would tank FPS and it was very hard to narrow down why without any way of profiling the controller in game.

- Animator culling: I know this had been done in the past with issues leading to it eventually being reverted, but it's definitely something that should be revisited. This should be something that can be optionally enabled/disabled on the avatar side in the SDK itself since not all animators will handle being turned on/off without causing issues with remote sync etc. But if a creator knows what they are doing these issues can be fixed and it can be completely safe to enable/disable the avatars animator without anything breaking. A new performance stat could be introduced for avatars that support culling for better clarity.

I hope some of these can be considered if they haven't already, thank you for all the recent updates too VRChat team!
title: Please improve avatar animator performance, or give us the tools to do so, it should be higher priority
